Bolsonaro then left Brazil through no regular border post, a police official said, and Trump aide Simon Levy confirmed political asylum in the US; Lula called the flight 'shameful'.

stocks:JPM.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, spanning Chase's consumer branches, corporate lending and one of Wall Street's biggest investment banks. Its results are read as a check on American borrowers.
stocks:JPM.recent: JPMorgan, in Lagos since 1961, won approval-in-principle from Nigeria's CBN to set up a merchant bank, the first step in licensing, though that decision does not account for the share price.

poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Peter Obi, the former Anambra governor who ran third in 2023, wins Nigeria's presidency in 2027. Its price is what traders will pay on an opposition upset of the ruling APC.
poly-will-peter-obi-win-the-2027-nigeria.recent: Tinubu launched his re-election bid in Kaduna with petrol costing about 1,400 naira a litre, and Microsoft said it would load Nigeria's candidate list into its AI systems. Neither concerns Peter Obi's own campaign, and nothing in the fortnight accounts for what traders will pay on him.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: What traders on Polymarket pay for a contract that settles at 100 if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate race. Ohio has leaned Republican in recent statewide contests, so the seat bears on which party controls the Senate.
poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.recent: The fortnight's news on prediction markets was about the platforms rather than the race: the CFTC sued Utah over its ban on Kalshi, and Polymarket pledged $3.9 million back to victims of a site compromise. None of it accounts for the shift in the Ohio odds.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win a majority in the US House of Representatives at the 2026 midterm elections. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and House control decides whether a president's agenda can pass.
poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.recent: The run-up to Election Day carried charges against ex-FBI officials over 2023 testimony, filed 11 days before the midterms, and a court's dismissal of Trump's lawsuit over the election in Alaska. Neither touches a House race, and nothing reported accounts for the price.

poly-netanyahu-out-before-2027-684-719-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu stops being Israel's prime minister before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with coalition crises, court cases and election timing.

poly-sudan-civil-war-ceasefire-by-decemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces agree a ceasefire before 2026 ends. The war, fought since April 2023, has driven the world's largest displacement crisis.

wiki-benjamin-netanyahu.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister. It rises with his elections, wars and trials, which have shaped Israel's politics for three decades.
wiki-benjamin-netanyahu.recent: Israel's election left neither bloc able to reach 61 seats without Arab parties, after high turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel. Polls had put Eisenkot 8 to 10 points ahead of Netanyahu. A day later Shin Bet said its probe did not implicate Arab voters, contradicting Netanyahu's fraud claim.

poly-will-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-win-.standing: A Polymarket parlay that pays only if three separate things happen: Lula wins Brazil's presidency, Gadi Eisenkot becomes Israel's prime minister, and Democrats take the US Senate. If any one leg fails, it pays nothing.
poly-will-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva-win-.recent: The Israeli leg did the lifting. Polls put Eisenkot 8 to 10 points ahead of Netanyahu going into the vote. High turnout among Palestinian citizens of Israel then left neither bloc at 61 seats without Arab parties. Shin Bet later said Arab voters had voted legally, contradicting Netanyahu.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Pakistan, the nuclear-armed South Asian state of more than 240 million people. It shows when world events send people looking for the country's basics.
wiki-pakistan.recent: Pakistan spent late October as a go-between on Iran. In Tehran, army chief Asim Munir was told that no enriched nuclear material will leave Iran, and Pakistani security officials joined Saudi and Turkish envoys there. At home, diesel passed Rs400 a litre and flour reached Rs150-170 a kilo, up over 200% since 2021.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: South Korea's largest company and one of the world's biggest makers of memory chips, smartphones and displays. It carries so much weight in Seoul's stock market that its share price moves the national index with it.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: Samsung is pulling fridges and washing machines out of Hong Kong months after quitting the mainland Chinese appliance market, keeping TVs and phones as Chinese brands take white goods. The share answers to memory chips instead: that business lifted it about 8% in a week before Thursday's earnings selloff on the Kospi.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire by the end of November 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each round of talks and each wave of strikes.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Trump's envoy Witkoff met Putin while Trump pressed Ukraine to cut a deal, and Ukraine paused its refinery strikes under US pressure. Then Lavrov said the war would continue and likely escalate, and the only truce that held was a four-hour window to evacuate Oleshky.

poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russia and Ukraine agree a ceasefire before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on talks, envoys and sanctions decisions.
poly-russia-x-ukraine-ceasefire-agreemen.recent: Bets on a truce rose as Trump's envoy Witkoff sat down with Putin, Trump told Ukraine to cut a deal, and Russia freed the American Stephen Hubbard. They fell back after Lavrov said the war would continue and likely escalate; the only pause since was a four-hour window to evacuate Oleshky.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Shares of the Cupertino maker of the iPhone, Mac and iPad, one of the world's most valuable listed companies. The iPhone earns most of its revenue, and its products are assembled largely in China on chips made in Taiwan.
stocks:AAPL.recent: Apple launched the M6 MacBook Pro and iMac, the Pro with a touchscreen, and John Ternus's first quarter as CEO set a record, with India driving iPhone growth. It also guided gross margin to 45-46%, down from 47.9%, as the AI build-out bids up DRAM and NAND, and said there would be no cheaper iPhones or MacBooks.

stocks:002236.SZ.standing: One of China's two largest makers of surveillance cameras and video systems, based in Hangzhou. US export blacklisting and an FCC equipment ban shut it out of American markets, so its sales lean on China and emerging markets.
stocks:002236.SZ.recent: The one item on Dahua's own business, a 2.63 billion yuan AI compute win, came after the fall rather than before it, and nothing in the input accounts for the decline itself.

stocks:RELIANCE.NS.standing: India's most valuable company, controlled by Mukesh Ambani: the world's largest refining complex at Jamnagar, the Jio telecom network and a vast retail chain. Its shares move with refining margins and Indian consumer demand.
stocks:RELIANCE.NS.recent: Reliance floated Jio Platforms: the offer raised Rs 30,188 crore, drew Rs 7.4 lakh crore in bids and listed 21.4% higher at $137.1 billion. Rubio pressed India's refiners to take more Venezuelan crude, tying its Russian oil waiver to a trade deal. RIL then had its biggest single-day gain since April 2020.

stocks:3988.HK.standing: One of China's four large state-owned commercial banks, and the most international of them: it clears offshore yuan in Hong Kong and other centres, so its shares carry both Beijing's credit policy and the yuan's spread abroad.
stocks:3988.HK.recent: Bank of China sold a 2 billion yuan Yulan bond in Dubai that drew 5 times demand, part of Beijing's push for yuan-denominated assets abroad. The sale came well after the share's high and low, and nothing reported about the bank accounts for its price.

stocks:ADANIENT.NS.standing: The flagship listed company of India's Adani Group, which starts new businesses such as airports, mining, roads and copper before spinning them off. Its share price is the market's read on the whole conglomerate's debt and governance.
stocks:ADANIENT.NS.recent: Adani Enterprises returned to profit in its latest quarter on its copper, renewables and airports units, and copper now supplies nearly 40% of its revenue. The results arrived after the share's slide, and nothing reported about the company this month accounts for the fall.

stocks:TTE.standing: France's largest oil and gas company, with production across Africa, the Middle East and the North Sea and one of the world's biggest LNG portfolios. Its share moves with crude and gas prices and refining margins.

stocks:DKNG.standing: A Boston-based online sportsbook and daily fantasy sports operator, one of the two largest in the US. Its revenue rests on which states legalise betting, how they tax it, and how much bettors lose each weekend.

poly-will-dan-sullivan-win-the-alaska-se.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Dan Sullivan, Alaska's Republican senator since 2015, wins the state's 2026 Senate race. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

stocks:JBLU.standing: The share price of JetBlue Airways, a New York-based US airline built around JFK and Boston, flying domestic, Caribbean and transatlantic routes. Fuel costs and its own debt load weigh on it more than on larger rivals.

stocks:TGT.standing: Shares of Target, the Minneapolis-based discount retailer with nearly 2,000 US stores selling groceries, clothing and household goods. Its sales read directly on how much middle-income American households will spend.

stocks:WMT.standing: The world's largest retailer by revenue, running supermarkets and warehouse clubs across the US and abroad. Its sales show what American households at every income level are spending on groceries and essentials.
stocks:WMT.recent: Walmart joined Eli Lilly and 36 other companies objecting to OKX and ICE trading tokenized versions of their shares, a refusal over who controls their shareholder records. It came after the rally and does not account for it; nothing in the input explains the climb.

stocks:WDS.standing: The Australian oil and gas producer behind the North West Shelf and Pluto LNG plants in Western Australia, shown here by its New York listing. Its earnings ride on Asian LNG contracts, most of them priced off oil.
stocks:WDS.recent: QatarEnergy agreed to buy up to 3 million tonnes a year of US liquefied natural gas through a deal with Woodside, turning to American supply as the Hormuz force majeure dragged on. The agreement was reported on 2026-10-29, after the last price on the chart, so it does not account for the move shown.

stocks:LLY.standing: The Indianapolis drugmaker behind the diabetes and obesity drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound. Their sales have made it the world's most valuable pharmaceutical company, so its share price is a running bet on the weight-loss market.
stocks:LLY.recent: Eli Lilly joined Walmart and 36 other companies in objecting to OKX and ICE's plan to trade tokenized versions of their shares. That leaves most of the issuers asked opting out, but nothing in the news accounts for the rise in Lilly's own stock.

stocks:ICE.standing: The company that owns the New York Stock Exchange, the futures market where Brent crude trades, and the clearing houses behind both. Much of its income comes from trading volume, so volatility tends to reach its share.
stocks:ICE.recent: The one story about ICE's own business cut against the share's rise: Walmart and Eli Lilly joined 36 other issuers objecting to the OKX-ICE tokenized stock venture, and most companies opted out of having their shares carried. Nothing else in the input accounts for the climb.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if no senior American and Iranian officials meet before 2026 ends. The two governments have met at that level only rarely since 1979, so a meeting would break a long pattern.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Three days of Qatari-mediated talks in Doha, with Araghchi there for Iran, ended without a deal, though Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 2 days of one and Trump said he would not strike after the midterms. A Qatari delegation then headed to Tehran to keep the mediation going, and US strikes hit Qeshm Island ahead of the vote.

stocks:CG.standing: One of the world's largest private-equity firms, based in Washington, running buyout, credit and infrastructure funds for pensions and endowments. Its earnings swing on the profits it books when it sells what it owns.
stocks:CG.recent: The only news here about Carlyle's own business came on 2026-10-29, after the last close shown: with the EBRD, it is selling Black Sea Oil & Gas, Romania's offshore gas producer, to Mazarine Energy as EU gas tops €100. That sale does not account for the earlier moves in the share.

stocks:SNP.RO.standing: Romania's largest oil and gas producer, listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange and controlled by Austria's OMV, with the Romanian state as a minority holder. It develops the Black Sea's Neptun Deep gas field with Romgaz.

stocks:SNG.RO.standing: Romania's largest natural gas producer, majority-owned by the state and listed on the Bucharest Stock Exchange. It owns half of Neptun Deep, the deep-water Black Sea gas project it is developing with OMV Petrom.

stocks:CART.standing: Maplebear is the company behind Instacart, the North American app that sends gig shoppers to pick and deliver groceries from supermarket shelves. It earns from delivery fees and from ads that brands buy inside the app.
stocks:CART.recent: DoorDash agreed to buy Instacart, which would fold the two largest delivery apps into one company and put the gig workers on both under a single employer. A takeover sets a price the buyer will pay for every share, and the stock moves toward it.

stocks:DASH.standing: DoorDash runs the largest food-delivery app in the United States and owns Wolt in Europe. Its share price follows order volume and the rules governing how it pays and dispatches its gig couriers.
stocks:DASH.recent: The one story about DoorDash's own business landed after the chart's last close: on 2026-10-29 it agreed to buy Instacart for $17 billion, putting the largest US restaurant and grocery delivery apps under one owner, with the FTC already probing how such platforms set courier pay. Nothing reported before that accounts for the slide.

stocks:RDDT.standing: Shares of Reddit, the US forum built from thousands of user-run communities, listed on the New York Stock Exchange since 2024. It earns from advertising and from licensing its users' posts to AI companies as training data.
stocks:RDDT.recent: Reddit lost over 1 million weekly search referrals in October as AI answers stopped sending clicks, and Steve Huffman told shareholders the site is moving to logged-in-only access. The wall serves two ends at once: keeping AI scrapers out and selling its data to them, at the cost of the search visitors who arrived without an account.

stocks:RTX.standing: An American aerospace and defence group whose Raytheon unit builds missiles such as the Patriot, and whose Pratt & Whitney engines power airliners and fighters. Its share moves on defence budgets and jet-engine output.

stocks:ABBN.SW.standing: A Zurich-based maker of electrification and automation equipment: switchgear, motors, drives and the control systems that run plants and grids. Its orders track what industry and utilities spend on power infrastructure.

stocks:6954.T.standing: Fanuc Corporation is a Japanese maker of industrial robots and the numerical controllers that run machine tools. Its orders track how much factories worldwide spend on automation, especially carmakers and electronics makers.
stocks:6954.T.recent: Trump set a 180-day clock on foreign robot imports in Washington, the first step toward tariffs on the machines Fanuc sells into American factories. That decision came at the end of the window, and nothing in the input explains the share's earlier fall.

stocks:6506.T.standing: One of the world's largest makers of industrial robots, servo motors and drives, based in Kitakyushu and listed in Tokyo. Its orders are read as an early gauge of factory spending in China and beyond.
stocks:6506.T.recent: Trump set a 180-day clock on foreign robot imports, which bears directly on the robots this company ships into the American market. That move came after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the earlier fall.

stocks:INTC.standing: The American chipmaker that both designs processors and makes them in its own fabs, the largest US bid at leading-edge manufacturing. Its share price answers to Washington's industrial policy as much as to PC and server demand.
stocks:INTC.recent: Intel beat revenue guidance and still lost 23% after hours, as PC chip sales plunged. The drop dragged down CPU rivals AMD and Arm and cost the US government about $10 billion on its equity stake. It landed as tech earnings fed fears about AI spending.

stocks:CRCL.standing: The company behind USDC, the second-largest dollar stablecoin. It earns most of its revenue from interest on the reserves backing each token, so its shares move with US interest rates and demand for stablecoins.

stocks:ESLT.standing: Israel's largest listed defence contractor, based in Haifa, making drones, artillery, electronic systems and munitions. Its order book follows Israel's own wars and European rearmament, and its share price answers to that backlog.

stocks:GM.standing: The Detroit carmaker behind Chevrolet, GMC, Cadillac and Buick, and one of America's largest by sales. Its profits lean heavily on pickups and SUVs sold in North America, so its shares are exposed to US car demand and trade policy.
stocks:GM.recent: General Motors agreed to pay $220 million after selling data from its Smart Driver system to brokers who passed it to insurers, but that news came after the latest price here and does not account for it. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting explains the share price.

stocks:4901.T.standing: The Tokyo-listed Japanese group that outlived the collapse of photographic film by moving into healthcare, semiconductor materials and imaging, in one of the best-known corporate reinventions in Japan.
stocks:4901.T.recent: Fujifilm is spending $63 million to quintuple its capacity for magnetic tape, a medium it first made in the 1950s. That report from Odawara is dated after the rise on this chart, so it does not account for the share price.

stocks:TSAT.standing: A Canadian satellite operator in Ottawa, long a geostationary fleet owner, now building Lightspeed, a low-Earth-orbit network for governments and businesses. Its shares weigh that costly build against the debt on its older satellites.
stocks:TSAT.recent: Telesat owes C$2.4 billion on its legacy geostationary business on 6 December, and its CEO told analysts he is 'pretty constrained' in what he can say about refinancing. That old business is shrinking, while Lightspeed, Canada's bet on a non-Starlink network, depends on the same company.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-michigan.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Democratic candidate wins Michigan's 2026 US Senate race, an open seat in a state that swings between parties. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and the seat counts toward Senate control.

poly-2026-senate-map-r-ia-ks.standing: A Polymarket contract on one exact combination of US Senate results: Republicans win Iowa and Kansas but lose Alaska, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. It pays only if all seven races land that way, and that demands a very specific map.
poly-2026-senate-map-r-ia-ks.recent: The fortnight's reporting on prediction markets was about their legal standing, not this outcome. The CFTC sued Utah over its ban on Kalshi, and Polymarket pledged $3.9 million to victims of a site compromise. Neither accounts for the price.

wiki-united-states-senate.standing: The upper chamber of the US Congress: 100 members, two per state, on six-year terms. It confirms judges and cabinet officers and ratifies treaties, so a one-seat majority can decide whose nominees get through.
wiki-united-states-senate.recent: The midterms close a Senate fight centred on two states. In Alaska, Trump wants Peltola prosecuted over a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, and the Justice Department sued to block certification only if the Republican loses. In Michigan, Trump called Senate candidate El-Sayed a jihadist days before the vote.

stocks:BIDU.standing: Baidu runs China's dominant search engine and has staked its next chapter on artificial intelligence: its Ernie models, its cloud business and its Apollo Go robotaxis. Its US-listed shares trade on Nasdaq.
stocks:BIDU.recent: The one recent report on Baidu's own business is a product deployment in Wuhan, where its AI agent turns residents' group chats into work orders. It appeared after the shares had already fallen and does not account for the price.

stocks:BABA.standing: The New York-listed shares of China's largest e-commerce group, owner of Taobao and Tmall and the country's biggest cloud provider. The price carries Chinese consumer demand, Beijing's regulation and US-China tension.
stocks:BABA.recent: Nothing reported in the window explains the slide. The one story about Alibaba's own business came after it: Apple is bringing Qwen to Chinese iPhones, announced from Hangzhou on 2026-11-01.

stocks:1024.HK.standing: Kuaishou runs one of China's largest short-video and livestreaming apps, the main rival to ByteDance's Douyin, and owns the Kling AI video generator. Advertising, livestream tips and e-commerce pay for it.
stocks:1024.HK.recent: Kuaishou's Kling closed a record round, raising 19.8 billion yuan for AI video, but that news arrived only after the last close shown here. Nothing else in the fortnight's reporting accounts for the fall in the shares.

stocks:0268.HK.standing: A Hong Kong-listed Chinese maker of cloud-based accounting and enterprise management software, sold largely to small and mid-sized firms. Its shares are a read on how readily Chinese businesses pay for software subscriptions.

poly-openai-1t-valuation-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, reaches a valuation of at least $1 trillion in 2026. OpenAI is privately held, so this is a rare public wager on what the AI boom's best-known lab is worth.

stocks:BX.standing: One of the world's largest alternative asset managers, investing pension and endowment money in private equity, real estate and private credit. Its share price rises and falls with deal activity, asset sales and the fees those funds earn.

poly-moodys-or-sp-downgrades-france-by-n.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Moody's or S&P cuts France's sovereign credit rating before its deadline. Those ratings feed into what Paris pays to borrow and which funds can hold its bonds.

stocks:LMT.standing: The world's largest defence contractor, maker of the F-35 fighter and Patriot interceptor missiles. The US government is its main customer, so its shares turn on Pentagon budgets, weapons orders and allied rearmament.
stocks:LMT.recent: Lockheed and the Pentagon struck an initial deal to produce 850 F-35 jets, reported on Oct 22. It is the one development here about the company's own business, and no report ties the share price to it directly.

stocks:AMGN.standing: A large US biotech company living on established medicines for bone loss, cancer and inflammation. Its share turns on patent expiries on those older drugs and on the pipeline meant to replace them.
stocks:AMGN.recent: The FDA moved to withdraw its approval of Tavneos, Amgen's vasculitis drug, saying the approval rested on manipulated data. That news arrived after the share's climb, so it does not account for the rise, and no other report about the company's business explains it.

poly-will-anthropic-ipo-by-november-30-2.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, goes public by the deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in cents on the dollar.

poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Gyanesh Kumar leaves office as India's Chief Election Commissioner by the deadline. The post runs national and state votes, and removal requires the same process as for a Supreme Court judge.
poly-will-gyanesh-kumar-be-out-as-chief-.recent: The pressure on him came from the opposition: Kharge said voter-roll revisions stole 4 state governments, and the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' march brought thousands to New Delhi demanding the election chief resign. Neither the charge nor the rally came with any step toward removing him from the post.

stocks:2317.TW.standing: Hon Hai, trading as Foxconn, is the Taiwanese contract manufacturer that assembles most of the world's iPhones and a growing share of AI servers. Its share price is a read on demand from Apple and the large data-centre builders.

stocks:ZURN.SW.standing: Zurich Insurance is a Swiss insurer selling property, casualty and life cover worldwide, with a large North American commercial book through Farmers ties. Its profits turn on catastrophe claims, pricing cycles and investment returns on premiums.

poly-france-declares-state-of-emergency-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether France declares a state of emergency. The 1955 law behind it lets the government impose curfews, ban gatherings and order house searches, and was used in the 2005 riots and after the 2015 Paris attacks.

poly-will-syria-join-the-mecca-agreement.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Syria joins the Mecca Agreement, a regional defence pact, within the contract's 2026 deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks Damascus's alignment with the pact's members.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-texas-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Republican candidate wins the Texas governor's race in 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state whose governorship carries weight on border policy and energy.

stocks:MDA.TO.standing: A Canadian space company that builds satellite systems, antennas and robotics, including the Canadarm arms flown on the Space Shuttle and the International Space Station. Its shares turn on large constellation contracts.
stocks:MDA.TO.recent: MDA Space agreed with Thales Alenia Space to build digital antennas for the first 66 satellites of IRIS2, the EU's secure connectivity constellation, under a €64 million deal announced on 30 October, as Canada and the EU explore Canadian participation. The deal came after the share's slide and does not account for it.

stocks:RIO.standing: One of the world's largest miners, listed in London and Sydney and traded in New York through depositary shares. Iron ore from Australia's Pilbara drives its earnings, which ties the share closely to Chinese steel demand.
stocks:RIO.recent: Rio Tinto halted underground operations at its Oyu Tolgoi copper mine, a stoppage at the project that carries the company's copper growth. The halt came only at the end of a slide that had begun weeks earlier, and nothing else reported over the period accounts for that earlier fall.

stocks:BHP.standing: An Anglo-Australian miner and one of the world's largest, listed in New York through American depositary receipts. Iron ore and copper drive its earnings, so its shares carry exposure to Chinese steel demand and global industrial activity.

stocks:NWSA.standing: Owner of The Wall Street Journal, The Times of London, HarperCollins books and a controlling stake in Australia's REA Group. Its value rests on Dow Jones subscriptions and property listings more than on newspaper sales.
stocks:NWSA.recent: A judge in Miami dismissed Trump's defamation suit against the company's Wall Street Journal and ruled that he cannot refile it. The ruling was reported after the last close on this chart, so it accounts for none of the price, and nothing else in the fortnight's news explains the share's move.

poly-will-helen-zille-be-the-next-mayor-.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Helen Zille, the former Cape Town mayor and Western Cape premier, becomes Johannesburg's next mayor. The city council elects the mayor, so coalition deals can matter as much as the vote.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-gov.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Democratic candidate wins Ohio's 2026 race for governor, priced as what traders will stake on that outcome. Ohio has elected Republican governors since 2010.
poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-gov.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting touched the Ohio race itself. What it carried was about the markets: the CFTC suing Utah over its ban on Kalshi, a Pentagon memo on insider bets, and Polymarket pledging $3.9 million to victims of a site compromise. None of it accounts for this price.

poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.standing: A Polymarket contract on Iran formally quitting the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty by 2027. The treaty lets a member leave on three months' notice, and leaving would end the legal basis for inspections of Iran's sites.
poly-will-iran-withdraw-from-the-npt-bef.recent: A lawmaker told Mehr that Iran's parliament would quit the nuclear treaty unanimously, yet the bets slid as diplomacy took over: Qatari-mediated talks in Doha, an offer to reopen Hormuz within 2 days of a deal, and Trump answering "no" on striking Iran after the midterms. US strikes on Qeshm Island followed on the eve of the vote.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: How many people read Wikipedia's article on bitcoin each day. Bitcoin is a digital currency with a capped supply and no central issuer, so price shocks, hacks and rule changes send newcomers to look it up.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: Chainalysis confirmed at least $5.9 billion stolen from Binance, a theft blockchain firms link to North Korea; Binance said it covered 90% of losses, and once withdrawals reopened users pulled a net $3.64 billion. Days later Mercado Bitcoin in Brazil halted withdrawals after $40 million left its wallets across 10 chains, with no public evidence tying it to Binance.

stocks:0020.HK.standing: A Chinese artificial-intelligence company listed in Hong Kong, known for computer vision and facial recognition and now also building large language models. US limits on its access to American technology and investors shape its business.
stocks:0020.HK.recent: SenseTime's one recent piece of news, the release of a model that runs 24 layers twice, came after the last close on this chart, so it accounts for none of this price.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before 2027; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. It asks about an invasion, a far higher bar than an air or missile strike.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Netanyahu pressed Trump to strike Iran after the midterms; Trump answered no, citing diplomatic progress, as a Qatari delegation headed to Tehran after three days of Doha talks ended without a deal. US strikes then hit Qeshm Island, one of the islands that guard Hormuz. That was an air attack, not the invasion this contract asks about.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-florid.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Florida's 2026 race for governor. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome in the third most populous US state.
poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-florid.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting is about the Florida race itself: the stories that touch Polymarket concern a site compromise, after which it pledged $3.9 million back to victims, and the CFTC suing Utah over its ban on Kalshi. Neither accounts for the price of this contract.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-south-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins South Carolina's 2026 US Senate race; its price is what traders will pay for that outcome. No Democrat has won a Senate race in the state since 1998.

stocks:RYA.IR.standing: Shares of Europe's biggest low-cost airline, based in Dublin and flying a fleet of Boeing 737s. Fuel is among its largest costs, so the oil price reaches its profits directly, as does how much of its fuel it has hedged.
stocks:RYA.IR.recent: Ryanair froze pay after saying it expects its jet fuel bill to rise €2bn next year. That news came after the last close shown here, so it accounts for none of this price action.

poly-will-jon-ossoff-win-the-2028-democr.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Jon Ossoff of Georgia becomes the Democrats' 2028 presidential nominee. The price is what bettors pay for that outcome, and it moves with his standing against the party's other contenders.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States ends its blockade of Iran by the close of 2026. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which is tied to whether Gulf oil reaches its importers.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Three days of Qatari-mediated talks in Doha ended without a deal, though Iran cut the time it said it would need to reopen Hormuz after one from 7 days to 2. Trump then answered "no" on striking Iran after the midterms, despite Netanyahu pressing him to; a day later, US strikes hit Qeshm Island.

stocks:MARUTI.NS.standing: India's largest carmaker, majority-owned by Japan's Suzuki Motor and built on small, affordable cars. Its sales are among the clearest readings of what Indian households feel able to spend on a big purchase.
stocks:MARUTI.NS.recent: Carmakers dispatched an estimated 525,000 cars to dealers in October, with Maruti leading the festive stocking. These are shipments to showrooms, not sales to buyers, so the figure records how much stock dealers took on for the season.

stocks:3690.HK.standing: China's largest food-delivery and local-services platform, listed in Hong Kong. Its shares answer to subsidy wars with rivals at home, Beijing's rules for platform companies, and the cost of expanding abroad.
stocks:3690.HK.recent: Meituan fit LongCat-2.5, a 1.6-trillion-parameter model, onto sub-80GB Chinese chips, while in Brazil over half of the Rio chain outlets targeted by its Keeta delivery arm were off-limits under iFood exclusives. Neither story accounts for the share price.

stocks:CA.PA.standing: A French supermarket group running hypermarkets and convenience stores across France, Spain and Brazil. Its thin margins make the share sensitive to food prices, household budgets and price wars with rivals such as Leclerc.

stocks:0941.HK.standing: China's largest mobile network operator by subscribers, controlled by the state and listed in Hong Kong. Its steady cash flow and dividends draw income investors, and its network spending drives orders across China's telecom and computing suppliers.

stocks:MRVL.standing: A US chip designer whose silicon moves data rather than running applications: custom AI processors, optical links and networking chips for data centres. Its fortunes rest heavily on the spending of a few large cloud companies.
stocks:MRVL.recent: The one story about Marvell itself is its $115 billion takeover of Lumentum, a company that began as a $1 billion spinoff, in a deal Nvidia's Huang is reported to have blessed. Bloomberg framed it alongside Meta's cross-border bond sale as AI debt. Nothing in the input explains the slide that came before the deal.

stocks:LITE.standing: An American maker of the lasers and optical components that carry data through telecom networks and inside large data centres. Its fortunes follow what cloud companies spend on AI infrastructure.

stocks:0728.HK.standing: One of China's three state-controlled telecom carriers, selling mobile, broadband and cloud services. Its shares show what investors will pay for a steady, dividend-paying state operator that is also building computing capacity for AI.

poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Israel-Hamas ceasefire is cancelled by Dec 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it reacts to fighting in Gaza and to the politics of the governments behind the truce.
poly-israel-x-hamas-ceasefire-cancelled-.recent: Traders bid cancellation up in the week Israel's election left neither bloc able to reach 61 seats without Arab parties, and US officials warned Gulf states of strikes after 3 November. Israeli strikes in Gaza went on, killing at least 5 Palestinians on Monday, without either side declaring the truce over.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States and Iran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by December 31. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on a waterway that Gulf energy exporters and importers depend on.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-decembe.recent: Three days of Qatari-mediated talks in Doha ended without a deal, and Iran cut its offer to reopen Hormuz from 7 days to 2. Trump then answered "no" on striking Iran after the midterms, with a Qatari delegation headed to Tehran, a day before US strikes hit Qeshm Island, which guards the strait.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers. The count shows when people outside the daily news flow go looking for the country, and its spikes point to events.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Ebola crossed into Nigeria as Kenya confirmed its ninth case. Nigeria evacuated one patient to Switzerland, and the NCDC widened health declarations for international travellers. In the same stretch Tinubu launched a re-election campaign under economic pain, and two more suspected cases were later isolated in the northeast.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve raises its policy rate by a quarter point at its December meeting. That rate anchors short-term dollar borrowing, so bonds, mortgages and currencies worldwide reprice around it.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The Fed held rates with a nod to December, a decision TD Securities had expected to draw 3 dissents. Warsh's muddled messaging afterwards revived doubts about the Fed's credibility, and traders were left to parse whether the hold was a pause before a December hike or the start of a wait-and-see stretch.

stocks:GILD.standing: Gilead Sciences is a US drugmaker built on antivirals, and among the largest suppliers of HIV medicines, including the twice-yearly prevention shot lenacapavir. Its shares turn on how long those drugs hold their pricing and on what follows them.
stocks:GILD.recent: A generic version of Gilead's twice-yearly HIV-prevention shot, lenacapavir, was cleared for low-income countries at an expected $40 a year instead of $28,218. That news came after the rise, and nothing in the input explains the share price.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares of the US electric-car and battery maker led by Elon Musk. Its valuation rests far more on promised robotaxis and robots than on the cars it sells today, so the stock often moves on Musk's plans as much as on its results.
stocks:TSLA.recent: Tesla reported on Oct 21 that net profit fell 43% to $787 million as margins shrank. The same day, SpaceX and Tesla were reported to be exploring a merger, and Barclays has since called a SpaceX merger "a key part" of the bull case for the stock, while other analysts argue the deal would be a bad move.

poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Washington and Tehran reach an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, on the waterway that carries Gulf oil and gas to the world.
poly-us-iran-hormuz-agreement-by-novembe.recent: Three days of Qatari-mediated talks in Doha ended without a deal, and Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz shrank from 7 days to 2. Trump then played down renewed strikes, citing diplomatic progress; a day later US strikes hit Qeshm Island and Bandar Lengeh, beside the strait, as a Qatari delegation headed to Tehran.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-maine-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins Maine's US Senate seat in the 2026 election, the seat Susan Collins has held since 1997. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: The Wikipedia article on the Houthis, or Ansar Allah, the Zaidi armed movement that has held Sanaa and much of northern Yemen since 2014. Its missiles and drones reach Saudi oil sites and Red Sea shipping.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: A Houthi drone hit Saudi oil at Shaybah, the Houthis claimed a strike on a pipeline, and an attack on Dammam airport killed two. The US ordered families out of Saudi Arabia, British Typhoons joined its air defences, Riyadh pushed its investor summit to 2027, and Saudi Arabia's defence minister then met Iran's president in Tehran.

poly-will-the-republican-party-hold-47-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Republicans finish the 2026 midterms holding 47 or fewer of the Senate's 100 seats, well short of a majority. That outcome would hand Democrats control of confirmations and the chamber's agenda.
poly-will-the-republican-party-hold-47-o.recent: In the run-up to Election Day, the news carried charges against ex-FBI officials over 2023 testimony, filed 11 days before the midterms; a court dismissing Trump's lawsuit over the election in Alaska; and Abdul El-Sayed's eve-of-vote rally in Detroit. None of it accounts for what traders paid.

wiki-united-states-dollar.standing: The currency of the United States and the world's main reserve and trading money. Most oil, debt and cross-border trade is priced in it, so its swings set borrowing costs and import bills far beyond America.
wiki-united-states-dollar.recent: Foreign flows into US equities reached a record on the AI boom, and that hot money tested the dollar's standing as a safe haven. The dollar's pull showed at the edges too: in Brazil, real futures fell 10% after Lula beat the market's pick, on fears for the fiscal deficit.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-iowa-s.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins Iowa's US Senate race in the 2026 midterms. Iowa has elected Republicans in every Senate race since 2014, so this contract shows how far bettors think that run is at risk.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-minnesot.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Democratic candidate wins Minnesota's US Senate seat in the November 2026 election. The state has not sent a Republican to the Senate in more than two decades.
poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-minnesot.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news was about the Minnesota race itself. The prediction-market stories were about who may run these markets: the CFTC sued 10 states, Utah among them, to protect Kalshi, and Polymarket pledged $3.9 million back to victims of a site compromise. Neither accounts for this price.

wiki-binance.standing: The Wikipedia article on Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume. Millions of retail traders hold funds on it, and much of the market's stablecoin and token liquidity clears through its order books.
wiki-binance.recent: Binance lost $6.3 billion in a record theft and later found more breach points than the one laptop it first blamed. The FBI pinned it on North Korea's TraderTraitor group, which Kim Yo-jong denies. Binance says it refilled 90% of the loss, but users withdrew a net $3.64 billion once withdrawals reopened.

stocks:SHA0.DE.standing: Shares of the Herzogenaurach maker of bearings, transmission parts and electric drives, one of Germany's largest car-industry suppliers. Its earnings follow carmakers' output and how fast the industry shifts to electric.
stocks:SHA0.DE.recent: Schaeffler is cutting 3,500 jobs and closing four German sites, with three quarters of the losses in Germany, as the crisis in Germany's car industry moves down the supply chain from the carmakers to their suppliers. The cuts were announced after the last price on this chart, so they do not explain its slide.

stocks:688036.SS.standing: The Shenzhen maker of Tecno, Itel and Infinix phones, sold cheaply across Africa, South Asia and the Middle East. Thin margins on low-priced handsets leave it exposed to the cost of the chips inside them.
stocks:688036.SS.recent: The one story about Transsion's own business was a cost squeeze: memory now exceeds 60% of the parts cost of sub-$100 phones, the segment it sells into. That pressure on margins runs against the rally, and nothing else in the input accounts for the rise.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-missis.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Republican wins Mississippi's US Senate seat at the November 2026 election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome in a state Republicans have held for decades.

poly-will-the-iranian-regime-fall-by-the.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Iran's Islamic Republic loses power before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, street unrest and rifts inside the ruling system.
poly-will-the-iranian-regime-fall-by-the.recent: Khamenei ordered commanders to answer any attack without geographic limits, Qatari-mediated talks in Doha ended without a deal, and US strikes hit Qeshm Island. None of it concerns the regime's hold at home, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by December 31. Roughly a fifth of the world's oil passes the strait, so the price is a bet on Gulf supply reopening.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: October ended with over 30 attacks on ships near Hormuz, a record, and with Iran's Revolutionary Guards claiming tankers hit mines on what they call unauthorized routes. Iran's offer to reopen the strait within 2 days of a deal was conditioned on the US lifting its blockade, and the US then struck Qeshm Island.

wiki-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva.standing: Brazil's president, a former metalworker and union leader who co-founded the Workers' Party and first held office from 2003 to 2010. He leads Latin America's largest economy, and the real trades on his fiscal choices.
wiki-luiz-inacio-lula-da-silva.recent: Lula overturned a first-round deficit to beat Flávio Bolsonaro by 4.4 million votes, days after a poll had Bolsonaro ahead 50.3% to 49.7%. Real futures fell 10% on the result, and Bolsonaro left Brazil through no regular border post; Trump aide Simon Levy confirmed political asylum in the US, which Lula called shameful.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company and the world's largest crude producer, with a small slice listed on the Riyadh exchange. The state owns nearly all of it, so its dividend is a pillar of the Saudi budget.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: Aramco's third-quarter profit rose 9% to $31.2 billion on a 35% higher average selling price even as its output fell. The Iran war shut the Strait of Hormuz, and the expanded East-West pipeline to the Red Sea let Aramco sell around the strait while its Gulf neighbours could not.

stocks:9984.T.standing: Masayoshi Son's Tokyo-listed investment holding company, which owns most of chip designer Arm and has staked heavily on OpenAI. Its shares trade as a leveraged bet on the value of those AI holdings.
stocks:9984.T.recent: The one story in these weeks about SoftBank's own business was a deal for Sceye to fly stratospheric cell towers over Japan, and nothing in it accounts for the slide in the share.

stocks:1810.HK.standing: Shares of Xiaomi, the Beijing maker of smartphones, home appliances and electric cars, listed in Hong Kong. It is one of the world's largest phone sellers, and its car business is the bet investors price on top of that.

stocks:603486.SS.standing: A Suzhou-based maker of home robots, best known for its Deebot robot vacuums, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. It competes for the same living rooms as Roborock and Dreame, and sells heavily abroad.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-kansas-s.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Kansas's 2026 Senate race. Traders buy and sell on that outcome. Kansas has not sent a Democrat to the Senate since the 1930s, so a price this high runs against a long record.
poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-kansas-s.recent: Nothing reported in the fortnight concerns the Kansas race itself, so none of it explains the price. The news about these markets was regulatory: the CFTC sued 10 states, Utah among them, to protect prediction markets, and Polymarket pledged $3.9 million back to victims of a site compromise.

stocks:SK.PA.standing: Groupe SEB, the French maker of Tefal pans, Moulinex and Rowenta appliances and WMF cookware, and the world's largest small-appliance company. Its share tracks household spending in Europe and China.

stocks:PHIA.AS.standing: Philips, the Dutch maker of hospital scanners, patient monitors and sleep-apnoea devices, listed in Amsterdam after shedding its lighting and appliance arms. A recall of its Respironics breathing machines weighed on it for years.

stocks:300866.SZ.standing: A Changsha consumer-electronics maker best known for Anker chargers and power banks, Soundcore audio and eufy home devices. Most of its sales are overseas, much through Amazon, so US tariffs and platform rules reach it directly.

stocks:BLK.standing: The world's largest asset manager, best known for its iShares exchange-traded funds. Its fees are a slice of the assets it runs, so its shares track markets and the flow of money into its funds.

stocks:MSFT.standing: Shares of the maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, one of the largest companies by market value. Its price now rides on whether heavy spending on AI data centres comes back as cloud revenue.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Microsoft offered buyouts to around 60,000 employees to contain costs, in the same breath as forecasting $175 billion in capital spending this year on its AI push. It is cutting payroll to pay for data centres, and the buyouts arrived while it was also planning layoffs.
